overview:
Not everyone wants nine-hour drives to the Sahara. This six-day private tour from Casablanca shows you Morocco's three great landscapes – mountains, desert and ocean – without ever spending more than about three hours a day in the car between sights. You base yourself in a riad in Marrakech for four nights, which means unpacking once, and from there you walk between Berber villages in the High Atlas around Imlil, watch the sun set over the stony Agafay desert from the back of a camel, and finish by the Atlantic in the white-and-blue port of Essaouira.

Most six-day tours on this route skip the mountains. We keep a full day in the Atlas because it is often the part travellers remember most: terraced valleys, walnut trees, earth villages clinging to the slopes and lunch in a family house with views of the highest peaks in North Africa. The Agafay evening gives you the desert atmosphere – camels, lanterns, a dinner under the stars – just 45 minutes from Marrakech, and Essaouira, a UNESCO-listed medina on the ocean, is the perfect slow ending before you return to Casablanca.

AT A GLANCE
• Duration: 6 days, 5 nights
• Start and finish: Casablanca (hotel, train station or Mohammed V airport)
• Nights: Marrakech (4), Essaouira (1)
• Type: private tour with driver, a licensed guide in Marrakech and a mountain guide in the Atlas
• Longest drive: about 5 hours (Essaouira to Casablanca, last day)
• Walking: easy to moderate; the Atlas walk is 3–4 hours on village paths
• Meals: breakfast daily and dinner at the Agafay camp; other meals depend on the package you choose

THE ROUTE
Day 1 – Casablanca to Marrakech (about 3 hours), optional stop at the Hassan II Mosque.
Day 2 – Guided day in Marrakech: medina, palaces, souks and the Majorelle Garden.
Day 3 – High Atlas: Asni valley, Imlil and a guided walk to the Berber village of Aroumd.
Day 4 – Free morning in Marrakech, sunset camel ride and dinner in the Agafay desert.
Day 5 – Marrakech to Essaouira via an argan oil cooperative; afternoon on the ramparts and port.
Day 6 – Essaouira to Casablanca, by the motorway or the slower coastal road.

WHY THIS ROUTE WORKS
• Short drives: no day has more than about 3 hours of driving except the return to Casablanca.
• One base: four nights in the same Marrakech riad, so you unpack once.
• Variety: city, mountains, desert and ocean in less than a week.
• Flexible: evenings and Day 4 morning are free, and every day can be adjusted because the tour is private.

WHO WILL ENJOY IT
First-time visitors with a week, families with children, couples, travellers who prefer comfort over long road days, and anyone arriving or leaving through Casablanca who wants to see more than Marrakech.

WHO MIGHT PREFER ANOTHER TOUR
If seeing the real Sahara dunes is a priority, choose the [7-day Sahara tour from Casablanca](/en-US/morocco/casablanca/tours/7-day-sahara-desert-tour-from-casablanca-marrakech-merzouga-dunes-fes/57a5dbebfaa010b8b01a1e2e), which includes a night at Merzouga. The Agafay is a stony desert, not a sea of sand.

PRACTICAL INFORMATION
Bring walking shoes for the Atlas and the medinas, a warm layer for the Agafay evening and the mountains (nights are cold from November to March), and a windproof jacket for Essaouira, which is breezy all year. The Majorelle Garden sells timed tickets online and often sells out; we book them for you when you confirm. Cash in dirhams is useful for entrance fees, lunches and tips.
descriptions:
What to expect: a gentle start – a scenic motorway drive from Casablanca to Marrakech, with an optional visit to the Hassan II Mosque and a first evening in the medina.

Your driver meets you at your hotel, the train station or Mohammed V airport. If your arrival time allows, start with the Hassan II Mosque, built on the ocean's edge and finished in 1993: its minaret rises about 210 m, and it is one of the few mosques in Morocco that non-Muslims can visit inside, on guided tours that run several times a day (not on Friday mornings). Then the motorway crosses the farmland of the Chaouia and the phosphate plateau before the first view of the High Atlas, often snow-capped in winter, announces Marrakech.

You check into your riad, a traditional house built around a courtyard, which will be your home for four nights. Your driver shows you the easiest way to reach Jemaa el-Fna, the main square, which fills at dusk with food stalls, storytellers, musicians and juice sellers. A rooftop café on the square is a calm place to watch it all for the first time.

SCHEDULE (times are estimates)
09:00 – Pick-up in Casablanca (or at the airport on arrival).
09:30 – Optional guided visit of the Hassan II Mosque (about 1 hour, ticket not included).
10:45 – Motorway to Marrakech, with a coffee stop (about 3 hours).
14:00 – Check-in at your riad in Marrakech.
18:00 – Free evening; walk to Jemaa el-Fna for dinner.

GOOD TO KNOW
• Mosque visits require covered shoulders and knees; shoes are carried in a bag.
• If you land in the afternoon, we skip the mosque and drive straight to Marrakech.
• Taxis cannot enter most medina lanes; a porter often carries luggage the last few metres to the riad (small tip).

INCLUDED: private vehicle and driver, airport or hotel pick-up, bottled water, riad with breakfast.
NOT INCLUDED: Hassan II Mosque ticket, lunch and dinner (unless your package includes dinners), tips.

Overnight: riad in Marrakech.
Meals: breakfast.

What to expect: a full day with a licensed local guide in Marrakech – the medina, two palaces, the souks and the Majorelle Garden.

Your guide meets you at the riad after breakfast. The morning starts at the Koutoubia, the 12th-century minaret that has been the city's landmark for over 800 years, then follows the lanes south to the Saadian Tombs, the richly decorated burial place of a 16th-century dynasty, and the Bahia Palace, a 19th-century vizier's residence of courtyards, painted cedar ceilings and zellige tilework. You cross the old Jewish quarter, the Mellah, with its spice market and a still-used synagogue.

After lunch in the medina, your guide leads you through the souks, each lane once given to a single craft: dyers, metalworkers, leather and slippers, carpets and lanterns. You see the Ben Youssef Madrasa, the 16th-century Koranic school with one of the most beautiful courtyards in Morocco, if it fits your pace. Late in the afternoon your driver takes you to the Majorelle Garden in the new town, the blue-walled garden of cacti and bamboo created by the painter Jacques Majorelle and later saved by Yves Saint Laurent, whose museum stands next door.

SCHEDULE (times are estimates)
09:00 – Meet your guide at the riad.
09:15 – Koutoubia, Saadian Tombs and Bahia Palace (about 2.5 hours).
11:45 – Mellah and spice market (about 45 min).
12:30 – Lunch in the medina (not included).
14:00 – Souks and Ben Youssef Madrasa (about 2 hours).
16:30 – Majorelle Garden with your driver (about 1 hour; timed ticket).
17:30 – Back at your riad.

GOOD TO KNOW
• Visiting craft shops is optional; your guide will never insist that you buy.
• Majorelle tickets are booked online for a specific time; we arrange them in advance.
• Comfortable shoes are essential: you walk about 6–8 km on uneven lanes.

INCLUDED: licensed local guide, driver for the Majorelle transfer, riad with breakfast.
NOT INCLUDED: entrance fees (palaces, tombs, madrasa, Majorelle), lunch, dinner, tips.

WHAT YOU'LL TASTE
Fresh orange juice on Jemaa el-Fna, msemen pancakes, and if you are curious, tangia – the slow-cooked Marrakech meat dish your guide can point you to.

Overnight: riad in Marrakech.
Meals: breakfast.

What to expect: a day in the High Atlas – a scenic drive to Imlil and a guided walk through Berber villages, with lunch in a family house.

You leave Marrakech in the morning and drive south across the Haouz plain. The road climbs through the Moulay Brahim gorge to Asni, where a large market is held on Saturdays, then winds up the valley to Imlil at about 1,740 m, the starting point for walks and climbs around Jebel Toubkal, at 4,167 m the highest mountain in North Africa.

In Imlil you meet your mountain guide, who was born in the valley. The walk follows mule paths through walnut and cherry orchards and irrigated terraces of barley and potatoes, crossing streams to Aroumd, an earth-and-stone village built on a rocky spur at about 1,900 m with wide views of the surrounding peaks. Your guide explains how families live here – the irrigation channels, the communal threshing floors, the shared ovens – and how tourism and agriculture now go hand in hand. Lunch is served in a village house: a tagine, salads, bread from the oven and mint tea on a terrace facing the mountains. In the afternoon you walk back down by another path and drive back to Marrakech.

SCHEDULE (times are estimates)
08:30 – Depart Marrakech.
10:00 – Short stop in the Asni valley and arrival in Imlil (about 1.5 hours driving in total).
10:30 – Guided walk through the orchards to Aroumd (about 2 hours).
12:30 – Lunch in a village house (about 1 hour, not included).
13:30 – Walk back to Imlil by another path (about 1.5 hours).
15:30 – Drive back to Marrakech.
17:30 – Back at your riad.

GOOD TO KNOW
• The walk is about 8 km with around 300 m of ascent; it can be shortened, and a mule can be hired for anyone who prefers not to walk uphill.
• From December to March there may be snow on the paths; your guide adapts the route.
• It is 10–15°C cooler than Marrakech: bring a warm layer even in summer.

INCLUDED: private vehicle and driver, local mountain guide, bottled water, riad with breakfast.
NOT INCLUDED: lunch in the village house, mule hire, tips.

PHOTO SPOTS
• Aroumd's houses stacked on the rocks with the peaks behind.
• The terraced fields and orchards in spring blossom or autumn colours.
• The Moulay Brahim gorge on the way up.

Overnight: riad in Marrakech.
Meals: breakfast.

What to expect: a free morning in Marrakech, then the Agafay desert at golden hour – a camel ride at sunset and dinner by candlelight in a desert camp.

The morning is yours. You might relax in a hammam, take a cooking class, visit Le Jardin Secret or the Yves Saint Laurent Museum, or simply enjoy your riad's roof terrace. Your driver can drop you anywhere in the city.

In the late afternoon your driver takes you about 40 km south-west of Marrakech to the Agafay, a landscape of bare, rolling hills of pale stone and earth with the snowy Atlas on the horizon. It is not the Sahara – there are no high sand dunes – but the silence, the light and the space feel a world away from the city. At the camp you are welcomed with mint tea, then ride a camel across the hills as the sun goes down and the colours turn from gold to pink. Dinner is served in the camp: salads, a tagine and fruit, often with Gnawa or Berber music around a fire, before you drive back to your riad under the stars.

SCHEDULE (times are estimates; earlier in winter)
Morning – Free time in Marrakech.
16:00 – Depart for the Agafay (about 45 min).
16:45 – Welcome tea and camel ride at sunset (about 1 hour).
18:30 – Free time at the camp; music by the fire.
19:30 – Dinner at the camp.
21:30 – Drive back to Marrakech.

GOOD TO KNOW
• Evenings in the Agafay are much cooler than in Marrakech, especially from November to March.
• Camel rides suit most ages; children can share with an adult and a cameleer leads every camel.
• If you would rather sleep in the desert, a night in an Agafay camp can replace one Marrakech night on request.

INCLUDED: private vehicle and driver, camel ride, dinner at the camp, riad with breakfast.
NOT INCLUDED: lunch, drinks at the camp, quad or buggy rides, tips.

PHOTO SPOTS
• Silhouettes of the camel caravan against the sunset.
• The Atlas peaks glowing pink at dusk.
• The lantern-lit camp after dark.

Overnight: riad in Marrakech.
Meals: breakfast, dinner.

What to expect: the drive to the Atlantic through the argan country, a visit to a women's cooperative and an afternoon in Essaouira's medina and fishing port.

After a last breakfast in Marrakech you drive west across the plains towards the ocean. As you approach the coast the land fills with argan trees, which grow naturally only in this part of Morocco. You stop at a women's cooperative to see how the nuts are cracked by hand and the kernels ground into oil for cooking and cosmetics, and to taste amlou, a spread of argan oil, almonds and honey. Along the road you may see goats climbing in the trees; some are genuinely feeding, others are placed there by herders who ask for a tip for photos.

Essaouira appears suddenly: a white town with blue shutters behind 18th-century sea walls, built for Sultan Mohammed ben Abdallah by a French engineer and listed by UNESCO in 2001. After checking into your riad, walk the Skala de la Ville, the ramparts lined with old bronze cannons, watch the blue boats come in at the fishing port and the gulls over the nets, and wander through the medina's galleries and thuya-wood workshops. In the evening, choose your fish at the grill stalls by the port.

SCHEDULE (times are estimates)
09:00 – Depart Marrakech.
10:45 – Argan oil cooperative (about 45 min).
12:30 – Arrival in Essaouira and check-in.
14:00 – Free afternoon: ramparts, port, medina and beach.
19:30 – Dinner at the port or in the medina (not included).

GOOD TO KNOW
• Essaouira is windy most of the year – good for kitesurfing, less so for sunbathing.
• The medina is compact and easy to explore on your own; a local guide can be arranged on request.
• Buying argan products at the cooperative is optional.

INCLUDED: private vehicle and driver, bottled water, riad or hotel with breakfast in Essaouira.
NOT INCLUDED: lunch, dinner, drinks, tips.

WHAT YOU'LL TASTE
Amlou and argan oil with bread at the cooperative; grilled sardines, sea bream and prawns at the port; a pastry from one of the medina's bakeries.

Overnight: riad or hotel in Essaouira.
Meals: breakfast.

What to expect: a relaxed morning by the ocean, then the drive back to Casablanca for your onward travel.

Enjoy a last morning in Essaouira – a walk on the beach, coffee on Place Moulay Hassan or a final look at the port. Late in the morning your driver takes you back to Casablanca. The quickest way is inland by the motorway, about 5 hours with a lunch stop. If you prefer, and if you have time, the coastal road through Safi, Oualidia and El Jadida is slower but beautiful, with a lunch of oysters by the Oualidia lagoon; tell us in advance and we will start earlier.

You are dropped off at your hotel in Casablanca, the train station or Mohammed V airport. For flights, we recommend a departure after about 18:00 on this day.

SCHEDULE (times are estimates)
10:00 – Depart Essaouira.
12:30 – Lunch stop on the way (not included).
15:00 – Arrival in Casablanca: hotel, station or airport.

GOOD TO KNOW
• The coastal option adds about 2 hours; we leave at about 08:30.
• If you have an early flight, we can leave Essaouira at dawn or move this night to Casablanca.

INCLUDED: private vehicle and driver, bottled water, drop-off in Casablanca.
NOT INCLUDED: lunch, tips.

WHAT YOU TAKE AWAY: mountains, desert, city and ocean in one easy week, with plenty of time to enjoy each of them.

Meals: breakfast.

faq.question: Is the Agafay a real desert?
faq.answer: It is a stony desert of bare hills and plateaus, not a sand sea. You will not see high dunes like those of Merzouga, but the landscape, the silence and the sunsets are genuinely desert-like, and it is only 45 minutes from Marrakech.

faq.question: How much driving is there?
faq.answer: About 3 hours on Day 1, 3 hours return on Day 3, under 2 hours on Day 4, 3 hours on Day 5 with a stop, and about 5 hours on Day 6. Days 2 and 4 morning have almost no driving.

faq.question: Is the tour private?
faq.answer: Yes. The vehicle, driver and guides are only for your group, so you can change the pace, add stops or rest whenever you like.

faq.question: Which meals are included?
faq.answer: Breakfast every day and dinner at the Agafay camp. Lunches and other dinners are not included unless your chosen package says so, which lets you try the many restaurants and street food of Marrakech and Essaouira.

faq.question: How hard is the walk in the Atlas?
faq.answer: Easy to moderate: about 8 km and 300 m of ascent over 3–4 hours on village paths, at a gentle pace. It can be shortened, and a mule can carry anyone who prefers not to walk uphill.

faq.question: Can we visit the Hassan II Mosque?
faq.answer: Yes, on Day 1 if your arrival time allows. Guided tours for visitors run several times a day except Friday morning; the ticket is bought on site. Shoulders and knees must be covered.

faq.question: Do we need to book the Majorelle Garden in advance?
faq.answer: Yes. Tickets are sold online for a specific time slot and often sell out. Once you confirm, we book them for you for Day 2.

faq.question: Can we sleep in the Agafay instead of Marrakech?
faq.answer: Yes. On request we can replace the Day 4 night in Marrakech with a night in an Agafay camp, so you wake up to the sunrise over the hills. There may be a supplement depending on the camp.

faq.question: Is this tour suitable for children?
faq.answer: Yes. Short drives, a camel ride, the Atlas villages and Essaouira's beach work well for families. Child seats are available on request and the Atlas walk can be shortened.

faq.question: What is the weather like?
faq.answer: Marrakech is hot from June to September and mild in winter, with cold nights. The Atlas is 10–15°C cooler and can have snow from December to March. Essaouira is breezy and mild all year. Spring and autumn are ideal.

faq.question: What kind of accommodation is used?
faq.answer: Traditional riads in the Marrakech medina and a riad or hotel in Essaouira, all with private bathrooms. The level depends on the package you choose (standard or luxury).

faq.question: Can the tour start or end in Marrakech instead?
faq.answer: Yes. As a private tour it can start at Marrakech airport and end in Casablanca, or the other way round. Ask us and we will adjust the days.

faq.question: Can we add the Sahara dunes?
faq.answer: Not within six days without very long drives. If the dunes matter, choose our 7-day Sahara tour from Casablanca, or add days to this one to include Merzouga.
